question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund reports a portfolio Beta of +0.35 against NIFTY 50. Which is the MOST accurate interpretation for a Cat III AIF board member?

answer.text: Portfolio Beta above zero always breaches SEBI limits.
The book is fully short; it will lose when NIFTY rises.
The book has a directional long bias; it will gain ~35 bps when NIFTY rises 100 bps, ignoring idiosyncratic risk.

explanation.text: The Logic: A positive Beta of +0.35 means for every 1% move in NIFTY, the book is expected to move +0.35%. This is a net-long tilt (long-short with directional lean), not pure market-neutral (would be ~0) and not short-bias (would be negative). The Trap: Option A ignores the non-zero beta. Option C gets direction wrong. Option B invents a regulatory cap on Beta — SEBI does not cap Beta directly, only leverage. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests same. XXI-B (PMS) uses Beta in long-only context. VIII (derivatives) tests Beta via portfolio Vol formulas. Manager's Pro-Tip: For a stated 'Market-Neutral' mandate, PPM typically specifies |Beta| < 0.2. Exceeding this trips an investor-disclosure event; re-hedge with NIFTY futures before EOD NAV strike if the rolling 30-day Beta crosses 0.15.
